      Undock and take the helm. Fly back within 7.5 km of the ring to dock again.

      Both powers keep liaisons on the Ring. Take up to three missions at once; bounties are paid when you dock, and every mission moves your standing: up with the side that pays, down with the side you hit. Orrin also pays a standing bounty on any warship you capture or kill.

        The War of Shattered Stars

        ━ Front line◆ Capital: never fallsBattle as reported■ Relay S/M/R/LDashed or faded: old news · Violet ring: the cage round the Old Void

        Who holds what as far as you know

        From the front

          Nothing here is live. Every report was carried: by a star carrier between relays, by a picket coming home, by an Orrin trader to Tarsis, or by you. The map shows each system as last reported; dashed and faded means old news.

          Intelligence

          Relay networks as far as you know

          Local relays connect their own system and sync only at the relay. Regional relays run a star carrier round the locals near them. Strategic relays are high command, joined by long-haul star carriers. Military relays take reports from pickets first, send a courier to high command with anything urgent, and can order reinforcements. Fly into range of a relay of a power that trusts you and you swap reports automatically: they pay in standing for news of the other side. Destroy a star carrier or a picket and its reports die with it, unless you strip its data core. A captured relay's whole database goes to the side that took it.

          Nothing here is for sale. Every upgrade is a part stripped from a wreck or a prize, carrying the tier of the ship it came from and its condition. Two parts of the same type and the same tier combine by adding their condition; different tiers will not mate. The yard can repair human-made (5th tier) parts only.

            How it works
            • Distances are in kilometres. Light here travels 30 km a second, so at 90 km what you see of a ship is three seconds old. Railgun slugs fly at a third to half of that; maser pulses at light speed; missiles are slow but steer.
            • Every ship is made of systems: bridge, sensors, guns, buses, reactor, jump drive, drive and more. Each has its own health. Where a round enters the hull decides what it breaks, and whatever survives is what you can strip and sell.
            • Click one of her systems to call a shot. The gunner aims at it and tells you the odds. They fall as the light gets older, the flight gets longer, her jinking gets harder and her speed across your line of fire rises.
            • Jump drives open a wormhole anywhere in range: other places in this system, or other systems in light years. Damping fields block them. A strong field stops the attempt; a weak one, a damaged drive or a jump made before full spool can tear the ship apart.
            • Disable her guns and keep her from jumping and her crew strikes. Strip what's left within 7.5 km and bring it home in your hold.
            • Nothing is for sale. Every upgrade is a part stripped from a ship, with that ship's tier and its condition. Each tier up roughly doubles what a ship can do to you, so to climb you have to beat ships above you. Parts of the same type and tier combine by adding their condition; different tiers will not. Worn jump drives add tear risk to every jump.
            • Two powers, the Concord (benign overlords) and the Dominion (a dictatorship), give missions here. Every mission and every kill moves your standing with both. Earn Trusted and that side's ships leave you be; spend standing on their rewards.
            • Click a point to set a course, then press K to micro-jump there inside the battlefield. It is quick, but the wormhole lights you up for everyone in the field for a good while.
            • Click a ship (or press P, or Follow in the Target window) to follow her: the helm closes to gun range and holds there. Press 4 to swing round under her stern at flank, V to keep after her while jinking across her shots, and P, Follow or 1 to break off.
            • When the fight is over, click a wreck and the Magpie flies over, slows and strips her. Shift + right-click more wrecks to queue them.
            • Stars and planets are real places: plot a jump to one from the jump plot. Their gravity damps wormholes, so leaving a low orbit or a close pass of a star carries tear risk.
            • Every part you fit is the actual piece cut from its maker's ship. The bridge you fit decides your hull: the human bridge flies the Magpie-class cutter; a bridge cut from an alien picket, frigate, destroyer or carrier means flying that ship's hull at full size (bigger hulls are tougher and hold more, but are slower, turn worse and are easier to spot). A higher-tier bridge brings a sharper crew. Name your ship at the top of the Fitting bay.
            • Complete a shipwright commission (Trusted rank) to restyle slots in looks you have salvaged before.
            • Some flash points have a Remnant lying between the fleets: a First Architect machine, dark and dormant. Every shot fired near it and every ship that dies feeds it; fill it and it wakes. Awake, it holds a damping field no one jumps out of and lances whatever is loudest, whichever side it is on. Run silent and it may pass you over. Its Heart is warded while its four lance nodes stand, and the nodes re-knit unless destroyed outright. Bring it down and cut out the Gate shard at its centre: a jump drive that ignores most of any damping field.
            • A Gate shard aboard rings on every jump, and the apex powers hear it. The louder it rings (resonance, in the Ship window), the likelier someone follows you: Seraphine Wardens, who hail and ask for it, or a Vorrakai hunt, who do not ask, and who will cut it from your wreck. Docking halves the resonance; a shard left in your stores does not ring. At the Ring, the Seraphine, the Vorrakai and a Myrr guild will each buy it.
            • Infamy (top of the station) grows with every ship you kill or capture, more for bigger and higher-tier ships, and a lot for a Remnant or a beaten hunt: Nobody, Noticed, Notorious, Feared, Dreaded, Legend. Ships talk to you on COMMS when they engage, when they are losing and when they strike. Big ships, high tiers and proud races sneer; small ships and nervous races are frightened, and more of them as your infamy grows. A ship that is afraid of you breaks sooner.

            Flying

            Left-click space Set a course to that point. R / F raise or lower the point before you click. 1 2 3 4 Engine speed: 1 Stop, 2 Slow, 3 Cruise, 4 Flank (fastest). Pressing 1 also breaks off a chase. V Evasive on or off: the helm jinks every couple of seconds and across any slug it sees coming. Harder to hit, but a little easier to spot. K Micro-jump to your course point inside this battlefield. Set a course first. It needs a working jump drive and charges like any jump; a strong damping field blocks it and a weak one risks tearing the ship; and the flash shows you to everyone here for about 14 seconds. M / J M opens the jump plot to pick another place or system. J jumps as soon as the drive can, even before it has fully spooled, which risks tearing the ship.

            Chasing a ship

            Left-click a ship, or P, or Follow Follow her: the helm closes in and holds at the distance in the box beside Follow, in km (blank: just inside gun range). Follow is in the Target window. Press P or Follow again (or 1) to break off; you keep your speed. 4 / V while following 4 swings round under her stern at flank speed. V keeps after her while jinking across her shots.

            Sensors (light is slow, so everything you see is old)

            Z Silent: no sensor pulses. You only see what other ships' own light and pulses show you, and you are much harder to find. X Active: your sensors pulse regularly. You see more, and fresher, but every pulse tells them where you are. C Ping: one strong pulse right now (switches you to Active). Good for a fresh fix on a target. Tab / T Tab selects the next contact. T turns the camera to face your target. Seen How old your picture of a ship is: big in the Target window, on the box around her, and in Contacts. Blue is fresh, yellow 3 s or older, red 10 s or older or a lost track. She has moved since.

            Gunnery (what your gunner is allowed to do)

            5 Hold fire: no shooting at all. 6 Disable: aim for her power buses first, spare ships worth taking as prizes, no missiles. Best when you want her parts. 7 Whatever it takes: every gun and missile, at whatever breaks her fastest. 8 Sink: destroy her. Click one of her systems In the Target window: call a shot. The gunner aims at that system and shows the odds of hitting the ship and that part. Strike craft Handled for you: whatever ship you have selected, the gunner pulses the maser at any hostile strike craft in reach, and the railgun stays on your target. Odds are best inside about 20 km. A fitted point-defence turret helps too. B Damping field on or off (if you have a projector fitted): ships inside it cannot jump away safely. It makes you louder.

            Salvage and docking

            Left-click a wreck The Magpie flies within 7.5 km, slows and strips her, most valuable parts first, until your hold is full or she is empty. Shift + right-click a wreck Queue more wrecks to strip one after another. G Near the station (7.5 km): dock. Near a wreck: strip it. Press again to recall the cutting crews.

            View and the rest

            Right-drag / wheel Look around your ship / zoom. The wheel over the scanner changes its range. Drag a title bar / – Move a window / collapse it. Reset layout (in Orders) puts them back. Space Pause (solo only). N / O Sound on or off / glow effects on or off (turn glow off on a slow PC). F11 / F10 Full screen / back to the menu.

            Help

            First sortie At the station (playing solo): a guided first mission against a lone deserter that walks through finding, disabling, stripping and refitting. Replay it any time. Report a problem In Orders, or at the station: say what went wrong and send it to the developer with the game's own log. You can read everything it sends first. If the game hits an error it offers this by itself.

            Help get it fixed ·

            Report a problem

            What gets sent: your words above plus the game's technical details
            
      
            What is in a report, and where it goes
            Nothing is sent unless you press Send report. Save and Copy keep it on your PC.
            In a report: what you type above; the game version and whether it runs in the app or a browser; the multiplayer state with captain names; where you are in the game, your ship and career numbers; frame rate; your graphics card's name, screen size and browser version; the last 30 comms messages; the game's own log of errors and warnings, including the end of the previous session; and in the app, the app's log of crashes.
            Never in a report: files from your PC, your saves, passwords, your PC's name, user name or address, or anything about other programs.
            Where it goes: to the developer's inbox through Formspree, a form service. Like any website, Formspree sees the internet address the report comes from. The game itself only holds the form's ID, never an email address.
            
      
            This copy can't send reports by itself. Save it as a file, or copy it, and send it to whoever gave you the game.
